title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. 𝔊 (written with a gothic letter, sometimes misread as 𝔖) is a profinite group. ρ and σ are two distinguished 'modular-type' elements or automorphisms; in the model case 𝔊 = SL(2,Ẑ) they are the standard torsion generators. Γ_{ρ,σ} is a group of (outer) symmetries respecting the conjugacy classes of ρ and σ, and γ_{ρ,σ} appears to be a further quotient (the margin defines SΓ_{ρ,σ} = Ker(Γ_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ})). Z_ρ and Z_σ are groups of symmetries fixing ρ, resp. σ, with structure maps δ_ρ, δ_σ to Γ_{ρ,σ}. B_{ρ,σ} has a map δ_B to Γ_{ρ,σ} whose kernel is L_0; the next page states this explicitly ('u ∈ B_{ρ,σ} tel que δ_B(u)=1 i.e. u ∈ L_0').

The previous page defined:
- SΓ^0_{ρ,σ} = B ×_Γ Z_ρ ×_Γ Z_σ, the triples (u,a,b) with δ_B(u) = δ_ρ(a) = δ_σ(b).
- A 'loop' set S𝒢_{ρ,σ}, consisting of pairs (α,β) in 𝔊 with ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} and η = βσ(β)^{-1}.
- A bijection (u,a,b) ↦ (ua^{-1}, ub^{-1}).
Transport of structure gives S𝒢 a twisted group law: (α',β')(α,β) = (u'(α)α', u'(β)β'), where u' is the automorphism with u'(ρ) = int(α')ρ and u'(σ) = int(β')σ. This is the same type of law as the Drinfeld–Ihara law on pairs (λ,f) in GT, or the law on 'solutions of the loop equation'.

This page does the following.
- (40) L_0 embeds in SΓ^0 by ℓ ↦ (ℓ,1,1).
- (41) Left translation by L_0 corresponds, on S𝒢, to the diagonal left action (α,β) ↦ (ℓα, ℓβ).
- (42) Define Γ^0_{ρ,σ} = SΓ^0/L_0 ≅ Z_ρ × Z_σ fibred over Γ (written γ).
- (43) Hence a canonical bijection Γ^0_{ρ,σ} ≅ L_0\S𝒢_{ρ,σ}. So the group Γ^0 parametrises loop-equation solutions modulo the diagonal L_0 action.
- (44) Put SZ_ρ = Ker(Z_ρ → Γ_{ρ,σ}) = Centr_𝔊(ρ), and likewise SZ_σ = Centr_𝔊(σ).
- (45) This gives exact sequences 1 → SZ → Z → Γ → 1.
- (46) and (47) give the extensions 1 → L_0 × SZ_ρ × SZ_σ → SΓ^0 → Γ → 1 and 1 → SZ_ρ × SZ_σ → Γ^0 → Γ → 1.
- The NB notes that for 𝔊 = SL(2,Ẑ) with ρ, σ modular one recovers the groups S_0Γ^0 and Γ^0 of §48 IX.

Purpose. This is part of an axiomatisation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller 'équation des lacets' situation. An abstract pair (𝔊; ρ, σ) replaces the modular case. The goal is to describe the symmetry group of solutions of the loop equation as an extension of a 'Galois-type' group by centralisers and by L_0. The next page then adds a G_{ρ,σ} component to build 𝓜^0.
errors: (44) second line: by symmetry it should read SZ_σ = Ker(Z_σ → Γ_{ρ,σ}) = Centr(σ); the manuscript writes SZ_ρ and Γ_{ρ,2}, a slip.
(45) first line: Γ_ρ should read Γ_{ρ,σ}.

Notational inconsistency between Γ_{ρ,σ} and γ_{ρ,σ}. (44) defines SZ as kernels to Γ_{ρ,σ}, but (42), (46) and (47) fibre over or project to γ_{ρ,σ}. For the kernels in (46)/(47) to be L_0 × SZ_ρ × SZ_σ and SZ_ρ × SZ_σ, the base of the fibre product must be the same group used in (44). The previous page's analogous sequence (42) uses Γ_{ρ,σ}, and the margin separately defines SΓ = Ker(Γ → γ). So either the lowercase γ is just Γ, or the kernels need adjusting.
Surjectivity in (45)–(47) of Z_ρ → Γ_{ρ,σ} (and of SΓ^0 → Γ) is asserted without justification on this page. It presumably depends on hypotheses fixed earlier.

SZ_ρ = Centr_𝔊(ρ) holds only if Z_ρ is the 'semi-direct' type group whose kernel to Γ is exactly the centraliser in 𝔊. If Z_ρ consisted of automorphisms and Γ were Out, the kernel would instead be the centraliser modulo the centre. This depends on definitions not visible here.

ideas.what: Group S𝒢_{ρ,σ} of pairs (α,β) solving a 'loop equation', with twisted multiplication (α',β')(α,β) = (u'(α)α', u'(β)β'), identified with a fibre product of symmetry groups.
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld–Ihara-type twisted composition law on GT-pairs; torsor/fibre-product description of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991), building on Grothendieck's Esquisse
ideas.where_published: The program is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme. The detailed 'équation des lacets' computations are in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation (this cote).

ideas.what: Quotient by the diagonal left action of L_0, giving Γ^0 ≅ L_0\S𝒢 and the extensions 1 → SZ_ρ × SZ_σ → Γ^0 → Γ → 1 and 1 → L_0 × SZ_ρ × SZ_σ → SΓ^0 → Γ → 1.
ideas.modern_name: Exact sequences for a fibre product of groups over a common quotient (kernel = product of kernels)

ideas.what: Axiomatisation replacing SL(2,Ẑ) and its modular generators by an abstract profinite group 𝔊 with two distinguished elements or automorphisms ρ, σ.
ideas.modern_name: Abstract 'GT-type' symmetry groups attached to a group with two distinguished conjugacy classes (cf. general Out-type groups preserving conjugacy classes of torsion elements)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related ideas in work on GT and on automorphisms of profinite free products

missed.claim: The page carries out, in an abstract (𝔊,ρ,σ) setting, the identification of loop-equation solution sets with fibre products of centraliser-extended symmetry groups, including the role of L_0. This generalises the SL(2,Ẑ)/modular case. It is part of a largely unexplored, unpublished axiomatisation of the GT-type loop equation, but this particular page is routine bookkeeping.
missed.quote: on trouve que (39) induit une bijection canonique (43) Γ^0_{ρ,σ} ≅ L_0\S𝒢_{ρ,σ}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as documentation of how Grothendieck intended to abstract the GT/loop-equation formalism beyond the modular case. Nothing on this page itself is a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine structural step: fibre products, kernels, and a quotient by a diagonal action. It sits inside an unpublished generalisation of the GT loop-equation formalism. That framework is of some historical interest, but this page contains no striking new result.
transcription_corrections: The base group, rendered 𝔖 in the transcription, is the same gothic 𝔊 as on the previous page (Centr_𝔊(ρ), 𝔊 = Sl(2,Ẑ)).
(44) second line, as written in the manuscript: 'SZ_ρ = Ker(Z_ρ – Γ_{ρ,2}) = Centr_𝔊(σ)'. The intended reading is SZ_σ = Ker(Z_σ → Γ_{ρ,σ}).
Margin note: 'SΓ_{ρ,σ} = Ker(Γ_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ}), S𝒢_{ρ,σ} = Ker(𝒢_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ}) = 𝔊_{ρ,σ} = ...'. The final term is uncertain.
Margin by (42): 'cf. Γ^0_{ρ,σ} dans §48, IX ff'.
The text after (40) reads 'translation à g.' (= à gauche); the subscript there is S𝒯'_{ρ,σ} / SΓ'_{ρ,σ}, and the notation fluctuates between Γ^0 and 𝒯'.
